behaviorDesc: Browses the thicket edges at dawn and dusk, stripping leaves and buds. The spotted summer coat goes plain brown in winter — same deer, different rumor.
description: a compact deer, white-spotted in summer, barking a sharp alarm
diseaseVector: Low risk — cook it through anyway.
huntText: A sharp bark from the thicket — the sika's alarm. It bounds in that rocking-horse gait, white tail flashing. It will circle back to check you; be ready when it does.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — lean, dark, excellent. The hide is tough and the antlers are trade. A sika feeds the village for days.

knowledgeLevels.1: Sika deer. Spotted in summer, barking like a dog when alarmed.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (lean), hide (tough), antlers (trade). Smaller than the deer you may know — a big stag runs 150 pounds.
knowledgeLevels.3: Hunt: dawn and dusk at the thicket edge. It barks, bounds, then circles back to look — the second look is your shot. Wind it and it's gone.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: sika hold tight in bamboo and burst late — walk the brake upwind and post a shooter on the far edge. Rut is late fall; stags are careless then.

name: Sika Deer
tell: a sharp dog-like bark, then silence — the white rump flashing through bamboo.
unknown: a spotted shape browsing the thicket edge

behaviorDesc: A night forager with a bandit's mask and a badger's build. Omnivorous and unbothered — it eats roots, frogs, persimmons, and your garbage, in that order of preference.
description: a stocky masked canid, grizzled and low-slung, waddling the night paths
diseaseVector: Can carry parasites — cook well, handle the pelt with care.
huntText: Rustling in the leaf litter, unhurried. The raccoon dog waddles the night paths with total confidence — it has never once been in a hurry, and that is its weakness.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — fatty, dark meat, and a superb winter pelt. The old name says tanuki; the pot says dinner.

knowledgeLevels.1: Raccoon dog. Masked face, stocky, out at night.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (fatty), pelt (superb winter fur). Not a raccoon at all — a true wild dog.
knowledgeLevels.3: Hunt: trap the night paths, or walk it up with a light — it freezes, counting on the mask. Snares on the runways.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: in hard cold it sleeps for days (the only canid that truly dens up). Find the latrines — it always goes in the same spot, and the spot marks the territory.

name: Raccoon Dog
tell: paired waddling prints and a latrine always in the same spot.
unknown: a masked shape waddling through the leaf litter at night

behaviorDesc: Roosts in the pines, feeds in the field edges. Explodes upward with a shattering cackle when pressed — the flush is the hunt's hardest second.
description: a long-tailed game bird, the cock iridescent copper-green with a white collar
diseaseVector: Low risk — cook it through anyway.
huntText: A cackle like tearing silk and the air explodes — the cock pheasant flushes vertical, copper and green flashing, then levels into a glide. You get one crossing shot.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — the classic game bird, lean and fine. The tail feathers are fletching and decoration both.

knowledgeLevels.1: Pheasant. Long tail, iridescent cock, white neck ring.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: breast meat (the prize), tail feathers (fletching). Hens are drab brown — learn both.
knowledgeLevels.3: Hunt: walk the field edges upwind; the flush is explosive but it glides straight after. Snare the dust-bathing scrapes.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: roost mapping — they return to the same pines. Evening flight lines are predictable. 2x birds with a posted second gun.

name: Ring-necked Pheasant
tell: a tearing cackle and dust-bathing scrapes at the field edge.
unknown: a long-tailed bird slipping through the field edge

behaviorDesc: One of the great birds — a six-foot wingspan of white and black with a bare red crown. Pairs for life and remembers faces. The old taboo says killing a crane curses the killer; the village will have opinions.
description: a towering white crane with black neck and a bare crimson crown
diseaseVector: Low risk — cook it through anyway.
huntText: It stands a head taller than you in the shallows, black neck curved, red crown bare. It has watched you since you were two fields away. The shot is long and the bird is watching.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — a great bird, and the village will talk about it for a year. The old people say a crane's mate mourns. Whether or not that's true, the feathers are magnificent and the meat is rich.

knowledgeLevels.1: Red-crowned crane. Huge, white, black neck, red crown.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (rich), the great wing and tail feathers. Endangered and revered — this is not a casual hunt.
knowledgeLevels.3: Hunt: only at need. They see everything; approach needs fog or a blind, and even then it's a long shot.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: the pairs dance at dawn in spring — bugling, leaping, wings wide. If you must, take a lone bird in hard winter, never a dancer, never a pair.

name: Red-crowned Crane
tell: a high bugling at dawn and footprints like a child's hand in the mud.
unknown: a huge white bird standing in the shallows, watching you

behaviorDesc: The most beautiful duck alive — the drake looks painted. Pairs bond hard; they arrive together, feed together, and leave together. Skittish to a fault.
description: a small duck, the drake absurdly colorful — orange sails, green crest, painted face
diseaseVector: Low risk — cook it through anyway.
huntText: A whistle of wings over the pond and they're down — the drake glowing orange and green among the reeds, the hen plain brown beside him. They'll flush at a snapped twig; move like water.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — small, rich, worth the stalk. The drake's feathers are worth more than the meat to a trader.

knowledgeLevels.1: Mandarin duck. The drake is impossibly colorful; the hen is plain brown.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (rich for its size), the drake's ornamental feathers (trade). Pairs for life — where there's one, there's two.
knowledgeLevels.3: Hunt: still-hunt the pond margins at dawn. They flush wild but circle back to the same water.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: learn the flight lines between roost and feed ponds. A blind at the landing end beats a stalk every time.

name: Mandarin Duck
tell: a soft whistling flight call and paired ripples on still water.
unknown: a flash of impossible color on the pond

behaviorDesc: Lives in troops with politics. Raids crops with military coordination — sentries posted, escape routes planned. The troop remembers who threw stones.
description: a heavy-bodied monkey with a red face and thick grey coat, watching you watch it
diseaseVector: Primates share our diseases — cook thoroughly, handle with care.
huntText: The troop moves through the canopy like weather — sentries posted, young carried, the old male watching you from a branch with total, insulting calm. They've raided the persimmons again. The question is whether the meat is worth the war.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — red meat, strong-flavored. The troop will remember this. Expect the sentries doubled for a month.

knowledgeLevels.1: Macaque. Red face, grey coat, troops in the trees.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (strong), the pelt. A crop-raider first, game second — hunt it as pest control.
knowledgeLevels.3: Hunt: the troop posts sentries; take the sentry's blind side or trap the raid trail. Never corner one — they fight.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: learn the raid routes between the sleeping cliffs and the orchards. A snare on the trail beats a fight in the trees. The troop adapts — rotate your sets.

name: Japanese Macaque
tell: sentries posted on high branches and a raid trail worn through the undergrowth.
unknown: shapes moving through the canopy with unsettling purpose

behaviorDesc: Hunts in disciplined packs — whistling to coordinate, running prey down over miles. Red-coated, white-tipped tail, utterly fearless of anything smaller than a tiger. A pack that has decided is a pack that does not stop.
description: a rust-red wild dog with a bushy black-tipped tail, moving in eerie silence
huntText: No bark, no warning — just whistles in the bamboo and red shapes flowing between the poles. The dhole pack has decided about the deer, or about you. Back away facing them; running starts the chase.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — lean red meat. The pack will know. Take it only if you can carry it home fast.

knowledgeLevels.1: Dhole. Rust-red wild dogs, hunting in silent packs.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat (lean), the pelt. They whistle to coordinate — an eerie, bird-like sound.
knowledgeLevels.3: Hunt: with great care. A pack defends a kill and investigates a hunter. Traps on the runways; never follow a pack into the bamboo.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: they run a circuit — learn the circuit and you're never surprised. They fear tigers more than you; tiger sign means no dholes that day.

name: Dhole
tell: bird-like whistles in the bamboo and a worn circuit of runways.
unknown: red shapes flowing silent between the bamboo poles

behaviorDesc: The mountain lord. An ambush predator that kills with a throat bite after a short explosive rush. Sees you long before you see it. The old rule: if you see it first, you might live.
description: an enormous orange-and-black striped cat, impossibly silent for its size
diseaseVector: Apex predator — the meat is the least of your problems. Cook it anyway.
huntText: The bamboo goes still in a way that has nothing to do with wind. Then the stripes resolve — shoulder-high, silent, watching you with amber eyes that have already decided. Do not run. Stand tall. Make noise. Be the thing it doesn't understand.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — you killed a tiger. The village will sing about this, and the songs will be true. The pelt is beyond price; the claws are trade and talisman both.

knowledgeLevels.1: Tiger. Enormous, striped, silent. The mountain lord.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: meat, the peerless pelt, claws and teeth (trade). This is not a hunt you plan — it's a hunt that happens to you.
knowledgeLevels.3: Survive: never run — running triggers the chase. Stand tall, shout, bang metal, back away facing it. It expects prey to flee; be the exception.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: tiger sign — scrape marks, a kill cached under leaves. Where a tiger hunts, nothing else dares. Some villages pay in food for the warning.

name: Amur Tiger
tell: scrape marks on the trail and a cached kill under leaves — where a tiger hunts, the woods go quiet.
unknown: stripes resolving out of the bamboo, watching you

behaviorDesc: The pond's vacuum cleaner — rooting the bottom mud for anything edible. The ancestor of every koi and goldfish; wild ones are bronze and built like bricks.
description: a big bronze deep-bodied fish rooting the pond bottom
diseaseVector: Low risk — cook it through anyway.
huntText: Mud boils up in the shallows where the carp are rooting — bronze backs rolling, tails flicking. They're too busy eating to notice you wading in.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — muddy if taken from still water, sweet from the creek. Bleed it fast and it's fine eating.

knowledgeLevels.1: Carp. Big, bronze, rooting the bottom.
knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: the whole fish — scale, gut, cook through. Creek carp taste cleaner than pond carp.
knowledgeLevels.3: Catch: dough balls on a hook in the shallows, or a net across the ditch. They feed hardest at dawn.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: chum the spot with rice for three days and the carp will queue up. Winter carp stack in the deep holes — find the hole, find the fish.

name: Common Carp
tell: muddy boils in the shallows and bronze backs rolling at dawn.
unknown: a bronze back rolling in the shallows

behaviorDesc: The small golden cousin of the carp — deep-bodied, bronze-gold, cruising the still ditches and pond edges. Humble, abundant, and exactly what a hungry village needs.
description: a small deep-bodied golden fish cruising the still edges
diseaseVector: Low risk — cook it through anyway.
huntText: Golden flashes in the ditch water — crucian carp cruising the edges in loose schools, sipping at the surface. A net, a line, or quick hands; they're not clever, just numerous.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — small but sweet. A string of them is a meal; a netful is a feast.

knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: the whole panfish — fry crisp, eat around the bones.
knowledgeLevels.3: Catch: bread paste on a small hook; they bite boldly. Ditch and pond edges at midday.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: they survive water that kills other fish — the stagnant ditch everyone ignores is full of them. Fish where others won't.

name: Crucian Carp
tell: golden flashes sipping at the surface of still water.
unknown: golden flashes in the ditch water

behaviorDesc: A snake-shaped fish that hunts the night creek — and whose blood is venom to anything that drinks it raw. Every culture that eats eel learned the same rule: fire first.
description: a long snake-like fish sliding through the night water
diseaseVector: Eel blood is toxic raw (ichthyohemotoxin) — cook the eel through, always. No exceptions.
huntText: A ripple with intent — the eel slides along the creek bottom, tasting the water. It takes a worm on a night line the way a secret takes a whisper. Land it fast; it ties itself in knots out of spite.
killText: About {kcal} kcal — rich, fatty, magnificent grilled. The blood is toxic raw, so the fire isn't optional: it's the whole recipe.

knowledgeLevels.2: Parts: the whole fish — but NEVER raw. Eel blood carries ichthyohemotoxin; cooking destroys it. This is not a suggestion.
knowledgeLevels.3: Catch: night lines baited with worm or fish guts; eel pots at the creek narrows. Handle with a cloth — they're stronger than they look.
knowledgeLevels.4: Mastery: eels run before the rains. Set the pots at the narrows when the water starts to rise and check at dawn. Bleed and grill over open flame — the classic unagi treatment.

name: Japanese Eel
tell: a purposeful ripple along the creek bottom after dark.
unknown: a snake-shaped ripple in the night creek
